solution.p: This equation is satisfied for x = 1/\sqrt{2} and x = -1/\sqrt{2}.

However, x = -1/\sqrt{2} is not in the interval [0, 2]. Thus the only critical number is x = 1/\sqrt{2}. The value of f at this critical number is f\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = - \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \approx -0.353553 The values of f at the endpoints of the interval are f(0)= 0 \quad \text{and} \quad f(2) = -{\frac{2}{9}} \approx -0.222222 Comparing these values we can see that the absolute minimum value is equal to - \displaystyle \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} and it is attained at x = \displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, while the absolute maximum value is 0 and it is attained at x = 0.
